topic: Rhi has just said, casually, that she always reads the last page of a book first, and of a box set she watches the final episode first, so she knows whether it's worth it. Jess has put her glass down.

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: Sorry, the last page? First? On purpose?

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: Course on purpose, why would I give eight hours to something and find out the dog dies?

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Does the dog die

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: Femi, don't encourage her.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: Hang on, so with Strictly you'd watch the final first?
T.full: Hang on, so with Strictly you'd watch the final first? Know who's lifting the glitterball and then sit through Halloween week anyway?

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: Don't need to, do I, it's whoever cries in week six, you could set your watch
T.full: Don't need to, do I, it's whoever cries in week six, you could set your watch by it.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: Week six? You've never watched it.

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: She doesn't need to watch it, she's been under half the sinks in town on a Saturday night. Gwen Price was crying so hard over some cricketer going out she let her charge
T.full: She doesn't need to watch it, she's been under half the sinks in town on a Saturday night. Gwen Price was crying so hard over some cricketer going out she let her charge double.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: Time and a half, Hugh. Saturday.

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: No, no, wait, go back, I'm not letting this go. The last page. Of a book. So what do you do with a whodunnit?

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: Read the end. Saves you guessing.

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: No, no, she's right, I'm, I'm with Rhi on this. Four hundred pages to find out
T.full: No, no, she's right, I'm, I'm with Rhi on this. Four hundred pages to find out it was the vicar, who has the time?

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: No, stop, stop, I went out with one of you. Before Matt. Lad called Craig, we're at the pictures, twenty minutes in he leans over, full voice, goes oh he's dead the whole time, I looked it up
T.full: No, stop, stop, I went out with one of you. Before Matt. Lad called Craig, we're at the pictures, twenty minutes in he leans over, full voice, goes oh he's dead the whole time, I looked it up. Twenty minutes!

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: Craig sounds like a sensible man.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Hang on, if he'd already looked it up, why was he there? Who picked the film, Jess?

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: Me. I picked it. And I still made him pay for the nachos before I binned him off in the car park.

backchannels.after: binned him off in the car park.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: You made

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: He spoiled it, Sunita!

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: Tall lad? From Knighton?

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: Wait, how do you know Craig? No, Hugh, don't do the face, what's he done?

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: He married our Bethan.

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: Shut up

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: Oh God, I fitted their boiler.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: So hang on, Hugh, she's binned your son-in-law in a car park and you've let her finish the story?

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: She's my niece, Femi. And he told our Margaret who done it in Midsomer before the first advert, so no, I wasn't stopping her.

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: So the one man in the Marches with any sense
T.full: So the one man in the Marches with any sense, and you've married him off and banned him from the pictures.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: Says the man who rang Kasia from the car park because he'd cried at the end of that dog film and couldn't drive.

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: Which is exactly my point! If I'd read the last page I'd have known about the dog and driven home like a normal man.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: So the dog does die, then.

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: Well, they generally do.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: My mum's worse than Rhi. Rings my auntie in Smethwick every Sunday, gets told how the Indian serial ends
T.full: My mum's worse than Rhi. Rings my auntie in Smethwick every Sunday, gets told how the Indian serial ends, then sits with us watching it going ooh, never saw that coming. Thirty years she's done that.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: See? Your mum gets it.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: No, but she doesn't watch it after, Rhi, that's the point, she just goes round telling everyone at the temple who's secretly the brother.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: No, that's not spoiling, that's a subscription. My mum would pay your auntie monthly for that, cash, no questions.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: No, but listen, if I'd read the last page of my marriage first
T.full: No, but listen, if I'd read the last page of my marriage first I'd, I'd still have the conservatory, wouldn't I.

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: You'd have rung me sooner.
